questions.prompt: A motor does \(600\,\mathrm{J}\) of work in \(4.0\,\mathrm{s}\). Find its average power.
A device transfers \(2.5\,\mathrm{kJ}\) of energy in \(10\,\mathrm{s}\). Find the average power in watts.
A \(40\,\mathrm{N}\) force acts in the direction of motion while an object moves at \(3.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the instantaneous power.
A force is perpendicular to an object's velocity. What is the instantaneous power from that force?
questions.answer:
The dot product is zero:
\[
P=Fv\cos90^\circ=0
\]

questions.prompt: A \(70\,\mathrm{kg}\) person climbs \(3.0\,\mathrm{m}\) vertically in \(5.0\,\mathrm{s}\). Find the average power output against gravity.
A \(25\,\mathrm{N}\) force acts at \(60^\circ\) to the velocity of an object moving at \(4.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the power.
A pump has output power \(800\,\mathrm{W}\). How much energy does it transfer in \(2.5\,\mathrm{min}\)?
A \(1200\,\mathrm{kg}\) car travels at constant speed \(15\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) against resistive forces of \(500\,\mathrm{N}\). Find the engine power delivered to maintain the speed.
questions.answer:
At constant speed, the driving force balances resistance.
\[
P=Fv=500(15)=7500\,\mathrm{W}=7.5\,\mathrm{kW}
\]

questions.prompt: A \(20\,\mathrm{kg}\) package is lifted \(12\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(4.0\,\mathrm{s}\) at constant speed. Find the average power needed.
A cyclist and bicycle have total mass \(80\,\mathrm{kg}\), climb a \(5.0^\circ\) slope at \(6.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\), and experience \(20\,\mathrm{N}\) drag. Find the required mechanical power.
questions.answer:
The cyclist must overcome the downhill weight component and drag.
\[
F=mg\sin5.0^\circ+20
\]
\[
F=80(9.8)\sin5.0^\circ+20=88.3\,\mathrm{N}
\]
\[
P=Fv=88.3(6.0)=530\,\mathrm{W}
\]

questions.prompt: A force \(\vec{F}=30\hat{\imath}-10\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{N}\) acts on an object with velocity \(\vec{v}=2\hat{\imath}+4\hat{\jmath}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the instantaneous power.
A machine delivers \(1.2\,\mathrm{kW}\) for \(15\,\mathrm{s}\). It raises a \(50\,\mathrm{kg}\) load vertically at constant speed. Find the height gained.

A \(1000\,\mathrm{kg}\) car increases speed from \(10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) to \(20\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) in \(6.0\,\mathrm{s}\). Ignoring losses, find the average power transferred to kinetic energy and the average net force over this interval.
questions.answer:
\[
\Delta K=\frac{1}{2}(1000)(20^2-10^2)=1.50\times10^5\,\mathrm{J}
\]
\[
P_{\text{avg}}=\frac{\Delta K}{\Delta t}=\frac{1.50\times10^5}{6.0}=2.5\times10^4\,\mathrm{W}
\]
Average net force from average acceleration:
\[
a_{\text{avg}}=\frac{20-10}{6.0}=1.67\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}
\]
\[
F_{\text{avg}}=ma_{\text{avg}}=1000(1.67)=1.67\times10^3\,\mathrm N
\]

questions.prompt: A motor with useful output power \(900\,\mathrm{W}\) pulls a box at constant speed \(2.5\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the pulling force in the direction of motion and the work done in \(40\,\mathrm s\).
questions.answer:
\[
P=Fv
\]
\[
F=\frac{P}{v}=\frac{900}{2.5}=360\,\mathrm{N}
\]
Work in \(40\,\mathrm s\):
\[
W=P\Delta t=900(40)=3.60\times10^4\,\mathrm J
\]

questions.prompt: A \(150\,\mathrm{kg}\) sled is pulled up an \(8.0^\circ\) slope at constant speed. The coefficient of kinetic friction is \(0.10\). A motor can deliver \(2.4\,\mathrm{kW}\), but \(15\%\) is lost to drivetrain inefficiency. Find the maximum constant speed.
questions.answer:
At constant speed, useful motor power balances gravity down the slope and kinetic friction.
\[
F=mg\sin8.0^\circ+\mu_k mg\cos8.0^\circ
\]
\[
F=150(9.8)(\sin8.0^\circ+0.10\cos8.0^\circ)=350\,\mathrm{N}
\]
Only \(85\%\) of \(2.4\,\mathrm{kW}\) is useful:
\[
P_{\text{use}}=0.85(2400)=2040\,\mathrm W
\]
\[
P=Fv
\]
\[
v_{\max}=\frac{2040}{350}=5.83\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}
\]

questions.prompt: A \(20\,\mathrm{kg}\) package is lifted \(12\,\mathrm{m}\) in \(4.0\,\mathrm{s}\), starting from rest and ending at \(3.0\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\). Find the average power transferred to the package and the average upward force exerted by the lifter over the interval.
questions.answer:
The energy transferred is gravitational plus kinetic:
\[
\Delta E=mgh+\Delta K
\]
\[
\Delta E=20(9.8)(12)+\frac{1}{2}(20)(3.0^2)
\]
\[
\Delta E=2352+90=2442\,\mathrm{J}
\]
\[
P_{\text{avg}}=\frac{2442}{4.0}=611\,\mathrm{W}
\]
Average upward force from average work over vertical displacement:
\[
F_{\text{avg}}=\frac{\Delta E}{\Delta y}=\frac{2442}{12}=203.5\,\mathrm N
\]
